finding: Names hold: Exhibit ONE's drawing (sharing side co: 6, 10, 9; observing side one: 2, 14, 17) and table spell 6-now-co-possibling, 10-next-co-possibling, 9-next-co-discovering, 2-now-possibling, 14-next-possibling, 17-next-existing exactly as the new text has them; Natural Naming 2.4 (lines 304, 330) gives the same split, sharing end 6, 10 across and 9 along, observing end 14 and its next 2 and 17 along. No dead (-ed) word, no dissolved word. But 'Its three each way are a self's six names between selves' as an identity parts from 4.4 three ways. (1) 4.4's six is the eight co names re-formed (ONE's co names 3-6 and 9-12); of the six names between selves only 6, 9 and 10 are co, while 2, 14 and 17 are 'one', so the six are not those eight re-forming and the 'one under two names' claim would be broken by a third naming. (2) 4.4's ways are 'a self sharing outward and its surface sharing inward'; the new text makes the inward way observing, and puts 9 and 17 along beside 6, 10, 2 and 14 across, which is not a surface sharing inward. (3) The second paragraph already says 'one same six' is three each way between a surface and its own 0, within a self; naming it also as between selves gives one six two homes. Also the six names carry no 'one at a time, sequencing, cycling' of their own in the files, so the identity is stronger than the files hold. The three-and-three shape of the six names is true and can stand beside 4.4 as a shape, not as the same six.
proposed_new: three phases each way, one at a time, sequencing, cycling. A self's six names between selves stand three and three beside it, as a sharing's two ends: sharing end 6-now-co-possibling, 10-next-co-possibling and 9-next-co-discovering, observing end 2-now-possibling, 14-next-possibling and 17-next-existing; they are not its eight co names re-forming.
